cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend. The Philistines are camped at Michmash, and in Saul's whole army only Saul and his son Jonathan even have a sword or spear (1 Samuel 13:16, 22). Then one day Jonathan turns to the young man who carries his armor and says, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.”

cards.question: Before he goes, Jonathan tells his father Saul about the plan.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Saul is staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron, on the outskirts of Gibeah. And his army? It's been shrinking for a while now (1 Samuel 13:8).

cards.question: Saul's troops with him at Migron number about ___ men.

cards.text: Ahijah is there too, a priest wearing an ephod. He's the great-grandson of Eli, the priest of the LORD in Shiloh.

cards.question: Saul's troops know that Jonathan has left.

cards.text: Now here's what stands between Jonathan and that Philistine outpost: a pass he has to cross to get there.

cards.question: The pass Jonathan plans to cross has ___ on both sides.

cards.text: And these cliffs have NAMES: Bozez and Seneh, one facing north toward Michmash and the other south toward Geba. Friend, the tallest thing I ever climbed in that junk drawer was a stack of old takeout menus, and I needed a nap after.
Jonathan turns to his armor-bearer again: “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men.” Then he says what he's counting on.

cards.question: Two men against a whole Philistine outpost. What does Jonathan say about the LORD?

answers.text: Nothing can stop Him from saving by many or by few
He only saves when the army is big enough
He will fight for them once Saul arrives

cards.text: Did you catch how he started? “Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf.” PERHAPS, friend. Jonathan doesn't know how this ends, but he knows Who can't be stopped.

cards.question: Jonathan just pitched a two-man attack on an outpost. What does his armor-bearer say?

answers.text: Go ahead because I am with you
Let us go back and ask your father
Let us wait until more men come

cards.text: With him heart and soul. Friend, I once asked the rubber bands I shared that junk drawer with to help me roll ONE pencil, and they told me they were busy. BUSY. We lived in a DRAWER.
Here's Jonathan's plan: they'll cross over and let the Philistines see them. Whatever the outpost says next tells them what to do.

cards.question: If the Philistines say wait until we come to you, what will Jonathan and his armor-bearer do?
And if the Philistines say come on up, what does Jonathan say that will be?

answers.text: Their sign the LORD has handed them over
Their sign to go back and get Saul
Their sign that the outpost is a trap

cards.text: The two of them step into view, and the Philistines crack that the Hebrews are coming out of the holes they've been hiding in. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for years, and even I felt that one.

cards.question: Moment of truth. What do the men of the outpost call out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer?

answers.text: Come on up and we will teach you a lesson
Wait there until we come down to you
Turn around and go back to your homes

cards.question: Jonathan tells his armor-bearer to follow him, because the LORD has delivered the Philistines into the hand of Israel.

cards.text: So Jonathan climbs up on his hands and feet, his armor-bearer right behind him. Hands AND feet, friend, straight toward the men who just promised to teach them a lesson.

cards.question: Jonathan makes it to the top of the cliff. What happens to the Philistines there?

cards.text: His armor-bearer follows and finishes them off, and they keep going, all inside about half an acre of land. That's not a battlefield, friend, that's a BACKYARD.

cards.question: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer strike down about ___ men.

cards.text: Then panic hits the Philistines everywhere: in the camp, in the field and among all the people. Even the outposts and the raiding parties are trembling.

cards.question: As the panic spreads, even the earth quakes.
Two men started it, but the text says where all that panic came from. The panic spread from ___.

cards.text: Over at Gibeah, Saul's watchmen look across and see the Philistine troops melting away and scattering in every direction. I bet Saul's standing there like somebody who hears the whole office cheering and has NO idea what he missed.

cards.question: Saul wants to know what's going on. What does he tell the troops with him?

answers.text: Call the roll and see who has left
Sound the horn and gather all Israel
Go and spy on the Philistine camp

cards.text: They call the roll, and two names come up empty: Jonathan and his armor-bearer. Then Saul says to Ahijah the priest, “Bring the ark of God.”
The ark was with the Israelites at that time. But while Saul is still talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp keeps getting louder.

cards.question: With the noise from the Philistine camp growing, what does Saul tell the priest?

cards.text: Then Saul and all his troops gather up and march out to the battle.

cards.question: When Saul's army reaches the Philistines, what do they find?

answers.text: Philistines swinging swords at each other
A Philistine camp left completely empty
Philistines lined up and ready to fight

cards.text: Saul marches out ready for a fight, and the Philistines are already having one... with each other. Total confusion, friend.

cards.question: Some Hebrews had gone up into the camps around them to join the Philistines. Now they stay on the Philistine side.
And the Israelites who'd been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim? When they hear the Philistines are fleeing, what do they do?

answers.text: Join the battle and chase them
Stay hidden up in the hills
Head back to their own homes

cards.question: So the ___ saved Israel that day.

cards.text: And the battle moves on beyond Beth-aven. Keep that apron on, friend, because this story's not done yet.

findings.problem: This is the first time Saul shows up in the lesson, but no card says who he is. Card 1 only mentions "Saul's whole army," and card 3 just says "Saul is staying under the pomegranate tree." The baker is never told that Saul is Israel's king.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: "Meanwhile, Saul is staying...", "And his army?" and "It's been shrinking for a while now."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says one cliff is "facing north toward Michmash and the other south toward Geba." In 1 Samuel 14:5, one cliff "stood to the north toward Michmash." That describes where the cliff is, not which way it faces.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new moment from the junk drawer: climbing a stack of takeout menus and needing a nap afterward. Jokes may only make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The card has four sentences: "Did you catch how he started?", the quote, "PERHAPS, friend." and "Jonathan doesn't know how this ends..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Did you catch how he started?" treats the baker as if they already saw the words "Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf." They didn't. Card 10 skipped that part of 1 Samuel 14:6, so this is the first time the baker sees it. It is true that Jonathan started this way, but the card suggests the baker missed something they were never shown.
findings.question: Can a story card point back to passage wording as if the baker already saw it, when no earlier card showed it?

findings.problem: The card has about five sentences: "With him heart and soul.", "Friend, I once asked...", "BUSY." and "We lived in a DRAWER."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new junk-drawer moment: the rubber bands refusing to help him roll a pencil. It also shows his drawer friends as unhelpful. That contradicts the backstory ("They were all in it together") and his character, since he never holds a grudge.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: "and they keep going" adds action the text doesn't give. 1 Samuel 14:14 reports only the first assault: about twenty men struck down in about half an acre.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Michmash" is a place. The right answer "God" and the other wrong answer "Jonathan" are both persons. Michmash is not the same kind of thing as the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This card mostly repeats earlier cards. Saul marching out was already told on card 13, and the Philistines fighting each other was the answer to card 14. The only new detail is "Total confusion."
